body.cap: LeapWave TX500/RX500 modules | Photo - LeapWave Technologies

body.x: Coaxial cables lose signal at high frequencies, and rectangular waveguides cover a wide range only by splitting it into multiple fragmented bands. LeapWave describes this as a critical high-frequency I/O bottleneck.

LeapWave Technologies S.L., a deep-tech company founded in 2022 and represented by Dr. Muhsin Ali, exhibited its interconnect and measurement hardware at the 57th Korea Electronics Show (KES 2026), held from Oct. 13 to 16 at COEX in Seoul. The company showed the Ultra-Wideband Sub-THz Source/Detector Modules (TX500/RX500) and the LW C500 microelectronic IC interface. It is seeking strategic research and development (R&D) and commercial partnerships with Tier-1 semiconductor manufacturers and foundries in Korea, as well as Test & Measurement (T&M) distribution partners.

LeapWave develops ultra-low-loss high-frequency interconnects and measurement solutions for advanced semiconductor packaging, including high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and co-packaged optics (CPO), and for 6G communications. Its core technology is the Dielectric Rod Waveguide (DRW), protected by six international patents.

In the TX500/RX500 modules, DRW technology allows continuous signal transmission from DC to 500 GHz through a single connector, according to the company. It reaches an insertion loss below 0.15 dB/cm across the entire spectrum, which LeapWave says delivers metrology-grade precision, while keeping backward compatibility with existing testing environments. The modules received the 15th KES Innovation Award.

LeapWave says its technology has been validated through Joint Development Agreements (JDAs) with advanced foundry leaders including NTT, ROHM and Fraunhofer HHI, and through ongoing partnerships with the instrumentation companies Anritsu, Rohde & Schwarz and Keysight. It adds that national metrology institutes including NIST in the United States and NPL in the United Kingdom have expressed strong interest and described the hardware as a potential "game-changer" for the industry.

LeapWave began commercial sales in 2026 and has recorded nearly EUR 100,000 in revenue, with a pipeline of up to EUR 150,000 in additional contracts under discussion. In first-year sales it supplied products to research institutions and industrial partners in Europe. The company, which is under four years old, exhibited at European Microwave Week (EuMW) 2026.

In September 2026, LeapWave became a core partner in the EUR 4.81 million Horizon Europe project LUMINA, which is developing 500 GHz hardware for 6G networks together with Thales and Telefónica. The company has also been officially selected for the EU Business Hub at Semicon Japan in December 2026.

LeapWave describes South Korea as its main target market, citing the country's role in semiconductor manufacturing, advanced packaging (HBM) and 6G telecom infrastructure. It is looking for two types of partners: joint R&D partners, such as Tier-1 semiconductor companies and foundries, who can integrate its intellectual property and hardware into next-generation packaging solutions, and specialized T&M distributors with technical sales expertise and local logistics capabilities.

In Asia, LeapWave is working with the Japanese semiconductor companies ROHM and NTT under strategic JDAs. Its goal is to raise Asia's share of revenue to more than 50% within three years, using KES 2026 to start partnerships with Korean semiconductor companies and foundries, followed by Semicon Japan in December 2026.

The 57th Korea Electronics Show (KES 2026) ran from Oct. 13 (Tuesday) to 16 (Friday) in Halls A and B at COEX in Seoul. The Korea Electronics Association (KEA) organized the show, and the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources hosted it. The KES website lists 500 exhibitors and 1,100 booths. Its themes included electronic parts and materials such as sensors, connectors, printed circuit boards (PCBs) and power supplies; AI transformation (AX) fields such as generative AI, on-device AI, AI chips and smart home and wearable devices; mobility; robotics; digital health; ESG; and Web 3.0 and XR. Alongside the co-located XR & Spatial Computing Show, the event featured X-SPACE 2026, a special exhibition covering digital twins, industrial XR, spatial intelligence, XR devices and spatial computing platforms. The Innovation Awards ceremony took place on Oct. 13.
